title: A Qutrit Time Crystal Stabilized with Native Chiral Interactions
summary: A driven chiral clock model of 9 qutrits shows period-doubled magnetization and a sharp subharmonic peak in the Fourier spectrum.
description: Reproduces Figure 2(b) qualitatively with a noiseless TensorCircuit-NG and JAX simulation of the driven chiral clock model. The original 15-qutrit experiment is scaled to 9 qutrits for fast local execution, while keeping the same Floquet structure U_F = exp(-i H0) exp(-i Hint) X^g, disordered chiral couplings, the spin-1 magnetization observable M = |0><0| - |2><2|, and the DTC-versus-thermal comparison. The microwave kick is modeled as the fractional spectral power of the qutrit shift operator X^g, which is an explicit modeling simplification used to obtain a smooth noiseless interpolation away from the exact g = 1 kick.

figures.target: Figure 2(b): Single-site magnetization traces and Fourier spectroscopy versus kick strength

title: Differentiable Maximum Likelihood Noise Estimation for Quantum Error Correction
summary: Surface-code noise parameters are recovered by differentiating through a CopyNode tensor-network contraction and optimizing with Adam.
description: Reproducing the differentiable maximum likelihood noise estimation for surface code using Tensor Network contraction with CopyNodes. The paper reports no single target figure for this experiment, so the reproduction reports the optimization convergence of the estimated noise parameters.

title: Entanglement Barriers from Computational Complexity: Matrix-Product-State Approach to Satisfiability
summary: Imaginary-time propagation of hard 3-SAT instances shows the MPS entanglement entropy peaking near the satisfiability threshold.
description: Figure 2 reproduction using the authors' Zenodo protocol (10.5281/zenodo.18743084): Weigt hard-satisfiable 3-SAT generator with p0=0.08, violation-vector Hamiltonian, and continuous tau optimization in [0,7.5] with the same sample-rejection criterion f(7.5) > f(10.0). Scaled down to n=4-15 (Panel A), n=8-10 (Panel B), 200 instances for feasible runtimes while preserving the core physics (linear entropy scaling and alpha_c peak). The bipartite entropy is obtained from a singular value decomposition of the propagated state on the JAX backend rather than from a tc.MPSCircuit.

figures.target: Figure 2: (a) <S_hat> vs n at alpha_c, (b) <S_hat>/n vs alpha

title: Exponential Quantum Advantage in Processing Massive Classical Data
summary: Quantum oracle sketching is compared with classical streaming and sparse baselines on an MNIST 3-vs-8 task at matched accuracy.
description: Reproduces the Figure 4(a) machine-size versus accuracy trade-off on a binary MNIST task (digits 3 and 8, 2000 samples per class, full 28x28 images reduced by PCA), comparing classical streaming, classical sparse representations, and quantum oracle sketching. A second experiment verifies the sample-complexity theory behind Figure 3(a) by evaluating the expected sketching unitary for a random Boolean oracle on 6 qubits and comparing its operator-norm error against the theoretical O(N/M) bound. That second experiment is diagonal operator algebra written with tc.backend array operations rather than a gate-level tc.Circuit simulation.

figures.target: Figure 4(a) - Binary classification machine size vs accuracy
Figure 3(a) - Boolean oracle sketching error scaling vs O(N/M) bound

title: Quantum Finite Temperature Lanczos Method
summary: Quantum Hutchinson states and a generalized eigenvalue problem give thermal energies of a 10-site TFIM without full diagonalization.
description: Reproduces thermal expectation values of energy for the Transverse-Field Ising Model using the Quantum Finite Temperature Lanczos Method (QFTLM). The original system size L=14 is scaled to L=10 for computational feasibility while maintaining the core algorithm logic (Quantum Hutchinson states and generalized eigenvalue problem).

figures.target: Figure 1(a): Thermal expectation of Energy <E> vs Temperature T

title: Quantum Continual Learning Overcoming Catastrophic Forgetting
summary: An 8-qubit amplitude-encoded classifier trained sequentially on MNIST and permuted MNIST forgets the first task as it learns the second.
description: This reproduction demonstrates catastrophic forgetting in a quantum classifier by training sequentially on MNIST (0, 9) and permuted MNIST (0, 9). We use an 8-qubit variational quantum circuit with amplitude encoding and 10 layers of hardware-efficient gates, with the layer sweep expressed through tc.backend.scan.

title: Efficient Classical Simulation of Random Shallow 2D Quantum Circuits
summary: Spatial Evolution Block Decimation contracts a random shallow 2D circuit as a PEPS-to-MPS sweep, checked against exact amplitudes.
description: This script implements the Spatial Evolution Block Decimation (SEBD) algorithm described in the paper for efficient classical simulation of random shallow 2D quantum circuits. Output amplitudes are compared against exact statevector amplitudes to quantify the truncation error as a function of the MPS bond dimension.

title: Data Re-uploading for a Universal Quantum Classifier
summary: One qubit re-uploads the input at every layer to act as a universal classifier, trained with L-BFGS on the JAX backend.
description: Reproduces the single-qubit classifier experiment (Figure 6) using the data re-uploading technique, with the layer parameters optimized by optax L-BFGS.

title: Differentiable Learning of Quantum Circuit Born Machine
card_title: Figure 6 · QCBM learning a Gaussian mixture
summary: A 10-qubit hardware-efficient Born machine trained with an MMD loss to fit a Gaussian mixture, differentiated end to end with JAX.
description: Reproduction of Figure 6: QCBM learning a mixture of Gaussians. The QCBM uses 10 qubits and a 5-layer hardware-efficient ansatz. The training objective is to minimize the MMD (Maximum Mean Discrepancy) loss with an Adam optimizer.

title: Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks
summary: quimb DMRG ground states feed a TensorCircuit QCNN that separates an SPT phase from the trivial one at N = 11 and N = 45 sites.
description: Reproduces the analytical QCNN phase recognition (Figure 2c) using exact ground states obtained from quimb DMRG simulation fed into a TensorCircuit QCNN through quimb2qop. Pauli sums are assembled with PauliStringSum2COO and the contraction is driven by a cotengra contractor.
